Saved. Reflection complete.

What this question exposed (genuinely generalizable):

The geometric mean of "percent change at an annual rate" data has TWO compounding traps, and I hit both:
1. You must convert each percent to a growth factor (1 + r/100) before taking the geometric mean — never geo-mean the raw percentages.
2. Because BEA quarterly GDP growth is published *at an annual rate*, each quarter must be de-annualized to a quarterly factor (1+r/100)^(1/4), and the result reported as a QUARTERLY percent — NOT re-annualized.

My answer 2.74 vs gold 0.69 is a clean ~4× ratio = exactly the annualization factor I left in. I geo-meaned raw annualized percents instead of de-annualizing to quarterly compounded growth.

Useful corollary I verified: the year RANKING is monotonic regardless of de-annualization, so the year (2017) was right — only the value was wrong. That's a good diagnostic for this question family.
